answer.text: Thank you, Tom. That is a valid point, and I agree with you up to a point. Phones do distract students, and nobody can deny it. But I see one drawback in a complete ban: many students use their phones to learn. For instance, last week my teacher asked us to record a short interview, and every group used a phone for it. Building on your idea, I would like to suggest a simple rule: phones stay in a box during explanations, and students can take them out when the teacher asks. Furthermore, we could ask the students to write the rules themselves. Seldom do people follow a rule that they did not help to make. Partly for that reason, I would not ban phones completely, but I would limit them clearly. Mia, what have you noticed with the younger children you work with? Do they need different rules? I would really like to hear your view before we decide anything.
accepted: Thank you, Tom. That is a valid point, and I agree with you up to a point. Phones do distract students, and nobody can deny it. But I see one drawback in a complete ban: many students use their phones to learn. For instance, last week my teacher asked us to record a short interview, and every group used a phone for it. Building on your idea, I would like to suggest a simple rule: phones stay in a box during explanations, and students can take them out when the teacher asks. Furthermore, we could ask the students to write the rules themselves. Seldom do people follow a rule that they did not help to make. Partly for that reason, I would not ban phones completely, but I would limit them clearly. Mia, what have you noticed with the younger children you work with? Do they need different rules? I would really like to hear your view before we decide anything.

Thanks, Tom. That is a fair point, and I partly agree with you, because phones really do distract us in class. However, I see a drawback: some lessons need a phone, for example to look up a word or take a photo of the board. For instance, yesterday we used a phone to record our science experiment. Building on your idea, I would suggest that phones stay in a bag, and that the teacher decides when we can use them.
